what_this_is: The Workshop row that makes one database login held by every computer the person names and gives its grants: one generated value, put to each computer's vault through secrets:put, read back by name, then the role made on the always-on computer.

payload.label: Make a database login held by every computer of mine
payload.job: Make one database login, held under one name by every computer I name, and give it its grants, so each computer can open the database through its own vault
payload.description: Generates one connection password in one process, puts the same connection string to each computer's vault through the engine's secrets:put (the person's own key, as keep-a-secret-by-name does), reads the name back on each computer, and only then makes the role with the login recipe (a-login) on the always-on computer, which holds the operator, and gives its grants as the database's owner (post-writer-for-a-login, or any grants recipe named). The password never goes into the answer, an error, a log or a tool run; the answer is {login, held_name, held_at, role_made, grants}. With make_role false it only puts and reads back, for a step that makes its own role.

login.description: The role name: letters, digits, underscores. Its connection is held as <login>-connection.

database.description: The database the login connects to and its grants apply in.

host.description: The database address the connection string names; the vault may send the value only there.

pins.description: Every computer's pin id that must hold the value. Given as input until each computer has its own row.

always_on.description: The pin of the computer that holds the operator login; it makes the role. Must be one of pins.

operator.description: The operator login's held connection name (CREATEROLE). Required when make_role is true.

grants.description: Optional grants recipe to run after the role is made, as the database's owner.

make_role.description: true (default) makes the role; false only puts and reads back.

invoke.stdin: the input JSON: login, database, host, pins, always_on, operator, grants, make_role. It holds no password; the tool makes it.
needs: the person's own sign-in (the sign-in command, or the Mac app's key)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Pipe the input JSON on stdin. Report only the answer.

provenance.source: New: the person's own door operation secrets:put (src/secrets.rs SECRETS_PUT), replacing the store-file write of `secrets put`.
provenance.note: Made by lane db-logins-every-computer, Nov 21 2026, from keep-a-secret-by-name's shape, for the fan-out of one generated login to every computer.
